title: Implementation Focus Check
description: Predict what an implementation checklist's done/todo counts actually tell you.

questions.prompt: What usually causes lost points on an "Implementation"-tagged problem?

options.text: Choosing an algorithm with the wrong time complexity
Missing one of the spec's rules, not picking a bad algorithm
Using too many helper functions
Submitting too early in the OA window

questions.explanation: Implementation problems are about completeness — most lost points come from an unhandled rule in the statement.

questions.prompt: In a checklist line like `[x] parse input`, what does the `[x]` marker mean?

options.text: The rule is still open (todo)
The rule has been marked done
The rule was skipped intentionally
The rule caused a runtime error

questions.explanation: `[x]` at the start of a line marks that requirement as completed; `[ ]` marks it as still open.

questions.prompt: A checklist shows `done=5 todo=0` but a hidden test still fails. What does that most likely mean?

options.text: The checklist counts are wrong
A "done" item was marked complete but implemented incorrectly
Hidden tests never relate to the spec
The checklist format itself caused the failure

questions.explanation: "Done" tracks completeness of coverage, not correctness — a covered rule can still be implemented wrong.

questions.prompt: Why does a checklist mindset fit implementation problems specifically?

options.text: Because these problems need a clever algorithm above all
Because success depends on covering every stated rule, which a checklist tracks well
Because HackerRank requires a literal checklist in the submission
Because checklists are faster to type than code

questions.explanation: Implementation problems reward completeness over cleverness, which is exactly what a rule-by-rule checklist verifies.

questions.prompt: Which line(s) count as free-form notes rather than checklist items, for counting purposes?

options.text: Any line not starting with `[x]` or `[ ]`
Lines starting with `[x]`
Lines starting with `[ ]`
All lines are checklist items regardless of format

questions.explanation: Only lines that start with the exact `[x]` or `[ ]` markers are counted; everything else is ignored as non-checklist content.
